Placeholder post to exercise executed code chunks: one static figure
(matplotlib) and one interactive figure (Plotly), both generated from
synthetic data at render time — nothing here is a real calibration result.

## Synthetic data

A toy binary classifier whose predicted probabilities are deliberately a bit
overconfident, so the reliability diagram below has something to show.

```{python}
import numpy as np

rng = np.random.default_rng(seed=7)
n = 2000

true_p = rng.uniform(0, 1, n)
overconfidence = 1.6
predicted_p = np.clip(0.5 + (true_p - 0.5) * overconfidence, 0.01, 0.99)
outcomes = rng.binomial(1, true_p)

n_bins = 10
bin_edges = np.linspace(0, 1, n_bins + 1)
bin_ids = np.digitize(predicted_p, bin_edges) - 1
bin_ids = np.clip(bin_ids, 0, n_bins - 1)

bin_confidence = np.array([predicted_p[bin_ids == b].mean() for b in range(n_bins)])
bin_accuracy = np.array([outcomes[bin_ids == b].mean() for b in range(n_bins)])
```

## Static version (matplotlib)

```{python}
#| label: fig-calibration-mpl
#| fig-cap: "Reliability diagram — a static matplotlib version."
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 5))
ax.plot([0, 1], [0, 1], linestyle="--", color="gray", label="Perfectly calibrated")
ax.plot(bin_confidence, bin_accuracy, marker="o", label="Model")
ax.set_xlabel("Predicted probability")
ax.set_ylabel("Observed frequency")
ax.set_title("Reliability diagram")
ax.legend()
ax.set_xlim(0, 1)
ax.set_ylim(0, 1)
plt.show()
```

## Interactive version (Plotly)

The same curve, but interactive in the built HTML — hover a point to see its
exact bin values rather than reading them off the axes.

```{python}
#| label: fig-calibration-plotly
#| fig-cap: "Reliability diagram — an interactive Plotly version."
import plotly.graph_objects as go

fig = go.Figure()
fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=[0, 1], y=[0, 1], mode="lines", name="Perfectly calibrated",
    line=dict(dash="dash", color="gray"),
))
fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=bin_confidence, y=bin_accuracy, mode="lines+markers", name="Model",
))
fig.update_layout(
    xaxis_title="Predicted probability",
    yaxis_title="Observed frequency",
    xaxis_range=[0, 1],
    yaxis_range=[0, 1],
    width=500,
    height=500,
)
fig.show()
```

@fig-calibration-mpl and @fig-calibration-plotly are built from the same
underlying bins, so they should visually agree — this is a check on the
pipeline, not a claim about the (synthetic) model's calibration quality.
